scope: GroupedFloat8Linear canonical block128 SM89 F32/BF16 native variants; admitted finite-zero weight case.
defect: The native grouped kernel formed As*Bs before scaling its code dot. Two individually finite F32 scales could overflow, turning an exactly zero weight/dot result into NaN.

witness.activation: 896 at index0, positive zero elsewhere; both F32 and BF16 inputs
witness.before: Actual SM89: successful Completion but 128 NaNs for each output dtype; same staged gtest exits1 as expected.
witness.after: Actual SM89 with new AOT: both output dtypes contain 128 zeros; original staged test object is reused.

fix: Keep pinned original_kernels.py unchanged. Apply existing runtime_top_k adaptation, then an independently hashed scale_order replacement: FP8 code dot, explicit mul.rn.f32 by As, explicit mul.rn.f32 by Bs, then original F32 outer accumulation/output conversion. No scale-domain narrowing, widened tolerance, new public precision policy, extra copy or executor.

canonical_regeneration.description: Actual product rebuild.py --stage gemm under WSL Triton3.8 completed successfully using the existing cache, with both new cubin SHA256 assertions inside the canonical script. No SDK rebuild.

source_freeze.lock_update: Root must update sglang vendored tree and NOTICE SHA256 after final AOT/header and compilation.json.

reviewer_execution.method: Offline reads, exact source adapter reproduction/hash checks, frozen ABI comparison, embedded cubin extraction, PTX dataflow and existing actual nvdisasm logs.

source_contract_assessment: The pinned original module is untouched and exactly hash-qualified. runtime_top_k then scale_order each apply to exactly one occurrence with before/after module hashes, including the intermediate input hash.

The changed branch is compiled only for the two qualified block128 FP8 jobs. Other source branches, quantizer, tl.dot, output conversion, sorting and actual launch signature/constexprs/options are unchanged.

Explicit mul.rn.f32 boundaries survive both PTX and inspected native images: no scale-product reassociation, no multiplication-plus-outer-add contraction, and no FTZ modifier on these arithmetic operations. The disassembly contains FTZ modifiers on unrelated float-to-integer indexing conversions; this is not evidence that scale arithmetic uses FTZ.
Logical scaling order agrees with the existing CPU dot-then-activation-scale-then-weight-scale path, but this review does not establish universal CPU/GPU bit parity.

test_assessment.semantic_witness: Positive zero FP8 weight codes, finite Bs=2^127, exact finite As=2 and exact quantizer input 896 avoid ordinary FP8 dot accuracy ambiguity. Dot-first zero remains zero, whereas As*Bs overflows before zero multiplication.
test_assessment.recorded_before: Root actual expected-red reports 128 NaNs for each F32 and BF16 output. The new product test calls actual SGLang prepare/submit/Completion and checks all outputs, not an emulated kernel.
test_assessment.after_execution: Not run by this reviewer; root owns current focused test execution.

limits: The FP8 MMA retains its original native numerical contract. F32 accumulator naming does not prove equivalence to IEEE sequential F32 multiplication and addition of decoded values.

This change guarantees the explicit two scale-multiply boundaries in the inspected SM89 variants, not finite output for every finite nonzero input or universal error bounds. Intermediate dot, first scaled product or final nonzero sum can overflow; underflow and native dot rounding remain possible.
The output conversion and outer add remain their original operations; no global fast-math or enable_fp_fusion setting was loosened, and no existing numerical tolerance was enlarged.
Source-fix.json records its pre-AOT handoff state; later aot-product-freeze.json and actual native logs are the evidence for generated artifacts.
No performance, end-model quality, other GPU architecture or full model claim is made.

numerical_boundaries.PTX_and_SASS: Both actual new variants retain 128 FMUL and64 FADD instructions around the original64 FP8 MMA instructions; reviewer verified scale dataflow and no FTZ on these arithmetic operations.
numerical_boundaries.unchanged: Pinned source, quantizer, FP8 MMA, two job signatures/constexprs/options, sorting, tile geometry, launch ABI and checked align payload.
numerical_boundaries.public_header: model_ops.h was not modified. CUDA user documentation describes the two scale multiplies and correct runtime slot domain.

archive_policy: Includes old-red logs/XML, same-test green logs/XML, recipes/identities, old/new source and embedded AOT headers, compilation/lock records, actual PTX/SASS and independent review. Excludes executables, objects, libraries, maps, scratch cache and cleanup records. Standalone cubins are not duplicated because their exact bytes are present in archived embedded headers.
limits: Five actual CUDA cases, zero skips: existing Direct/Graph/runtime-slot/checked-ID coverage, product semantic regression and original staged witness.
CPU source establishes the scaling order; this batch did not execute new CPU, Apple or Vulkan tests and does not prove universal cross-platform bit parity.
Native FP8 MMA keeps its original numerical behavior. F32 accumulation naming does not prove ordinary decoded IEEE F32 MatMul equivalence.
This fixes an admitted finite-zero-weight defect. Nonzero dot, scaled products or sums can still overflow; no finite-output guarantee for all finite inputs is claimed.
No selected FP8 artifact/full model execution, model quality evaluation, throughput test, other GPU architecture or peak-memory measurement was performed for this fix.
